newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: OMAR UNOPPOSED FOR S.AFRICA'S ANC IN WESTERN CAPE.
newsitem.headline: OMAR UNOPPOSED FOR S.AFRICA'S ANC IN WESTERN CAPE.

text.p: African National Congress (ANC) firebrand Tony Yengeni and Western Cape health minister Ebrahim Rasool pulled out of the race for provincial leader on Friday, leaving Justice Minister Dullah Omar a clear field.
The Western Cape region of the ANC meets on Saturday for a conference including the election of a successor to provincial leader Chris Nissen, who has resigned.
Rasool, who was forced recently to apologise to Omar for criticising his effectiveness, announced on Friday that he had dropped out of the race.
Yengeni told Reuters later he had withdrawn his candidacy as chairman and deputy chairman because it had become clear that Omar was "the best man for the job".
He said the key issue was for the ANC to consolidate its support ahead of the 1999 election.
"It is a scandal that the National Party is still in power in the Western Cape after everything it did in this country. It gives me nightmares.
"The central issue for the ANC in the Western Cape must be to win the election in 1999," he said.
Yengeni said he might concentrate more in the future on a national career, but said he had not made any final decision.

"It has always been my view that there should be no contest for the chairmanship of the party. I subscribe to democracy, but the division that this sort of contest could cause lives on long after the conference is over," he said.

The tide turned against Yengeni, a member of parliament and chairman of the powerful Standing Committee on Defence, when the ANC Youth league backed Omar for the leadership and nominated him as deputy chairman.
Yengeni said he did not believe it would be appropriate to have two national politicians who are both members of the ANC's National Executive Committee as provincial leaders.
He said he would support Omar for the leadership and Cape Town executive committee chairwoman Nomaindia Mfeketo as deputy leader in the Western Cape.
The National Party last week elected Western Cape Premier Hernus Kriel as provincial leader in place of Dawie de Villiers, who retired.
